company_description: MGM Resorts International, through its subsidiaries, operates as a gaming and entertainment company in the United States, China, and internationally. It operates through four segments: Las Vegas Strip Resorts, Regional Operations, MGM China, and MGM Digital. The company operates casino resorts that offer gaming, hotel, convention, dining, entertainment, retail, and other resort amenities, as well as online/digital games through its online platforms. Its casino operations include slots and table games, as well as live dealer, online sports betting, and iGaming through BetMGM. The company's customers include premium gaming customers; leisure and wholesale travel customers; business travelers; and group customers, including conventions, trade associations, and small meetings. The company was formerly known as MGM MIRAGE and changed its name to MGM Resorts International in June 2010. MGM Resorts International was incorporated in 1986 and is based in Las Vegas, Nevada.

risks.title: Cybersecurity
risks.summary: The company is exposed to cybersecurity risks that could have a significant impact on its operations and reputation. A prior incident occurred in 2023.
risks.score_rationale: The company explicitly mentions risks related to cybersecurity, including data loss and unauthorized access. A significant cybersecurity incident in September 2023 caused operational disruptions. The appointment of a Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) demonstrates that this risk is taken seriously at the board level. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Regulation
risks.summary: Changes in gaming laws and regulations could materially impact the company's operations, particularly in Macau.
risks.score_rationale: The company operates in a highly regulated industry. Major changes in Macau's gaming law in 2022, including a maximum 10-year concession limit, demonstrate significant regulatory exposure. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Competition
risks.summary: Increased competition in land-based and online gaming could impact the company's growth and profitability.
risks.score_rationale: The company operates in a highly competitive sector. The non-renewal of the commercial gaming license for Empire City in 2025 and the sale of several properties (The Mirage, Gold Strike Tunica, MGM Northfield Park) reflect competitive pressures. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Technology Dependence
risks.summary: Technology failures or technical issues could disrupt critical casino and hotel operations.
risks.score_rationale: The company relies on technology to operate its gaming and hospitality activities. Technical failures could impact operations. Cybersecurity infrastructure is being strengthened with an ongoing search for a new CISO. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Geopolitical
risks.summary: Changes in the geopolitical situation in Asia could affect operations and demand at Macau properties.
risks.score_rationale: The company has significant operations in Asia, particularly in Macau via MGM China (56% ownership). Regional geopolitical changes could affect operations and visitor demand. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Litigation
risks.summary: Litigation and legal proceedings could impact operations and reputation.
risks.score_rationale: The company is a large enterprise operating in a regulated sector and may be exposed to litigation. The mention of a 2023 cybersecurity incident could potentially lead to claims. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Reputation
risks.summary: Reputational risks could impact the company's ability to attract and retain customers.
risks.score_rationale: The company faces reputational risks related to cybersecurity, gaming operations, and customer attraction. The 2023 cybersecurity incident resulted in remediation costs. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Financial and Market Risk
risks.summary: Changes in market conditions and consumer trends could affect revenues and profitability.
risks.score_rationale: The company has adopted an asset-light model and generated $17.5 billion in revenue in 2025. Changes in market conditions could affect demand and profitability. Property sales reflect active portfolio management. (default score, to be refined)
